### Supplier delivery import and constructor audit

The [detailed example README](../examples/focus-functions/README.md) explains full input/output, field responsibilities, failures and compatibility. It links every published file and the [49-name audit inventory](../audit-focus-constructors.json). The new audit adds **508 executable checks** (including representative types, context/error/cardinality cases, 3.1 alternatives and experimental outcomes); the original three checks remain.

Input:

```xml
<deliveries><line id="A" quantity="12" price="2.50" date="2026-10-12" active="true"/><line id="B" quantity="5" price="4.00" date="2026-10-13" active="false"/></deliveries>
```

Complete [4.0 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-40.xpath):

```xquery
string-join(for $line in parse-xml('<deliveries><line id="A" quantity="12" price="2.50" date="2026-10-12" active="true"/><line id="B" quantity="5" price="4.00" date="2026-10-13" active="false"/></deliveries>')/deliveries/line return concat($line/@id, '|', $line/@quantity ! xs:integer(), '|', $line/@price ! xs:decimal(), '|', $line/@date ! xs:date(), '|', $line/@active ! xs:boolean()), ';')
```

Output (id, quantity, price, promised date, active flag):

```text
A|12|2.5|2026-10-12|true;B|5|4|2026-10-13|false
```

The [3.1 report](../examples/focus-functions/audit/import-31.xpath) uses explicit `(.)` constructor arguments and produces identical output. Both empty-input reports return an empty string; reordered input retains document order. Quantity `twelve` refuses FORG0001 in both versions. These reports normalize values; they do not apply required-field, schema or business-total validation.

Empty simple-map input means no call occurs. It differs from a missing context item (XPDY0002 for every zero-arity constructor), explicit empty argument (empty result for every one-argument constructor), and a multi-item argument (tested integer refusal XPTY0004). Mapping two lexical inputs invokes the constructor once per item: scalar types produce two values; ENTITIES/IDREFS/NMTOKENS produce four for two two-token inputs.

All 48 inhabited types pass representative value/type checks. `xs:error` is registered but has no non-empty value space; its non-empty calls refuse FORG0001 and its explicit empty argument returns empty. This is not a missing constructor implementation. String-like types have no generic invalid lexical string; their invalid-input checks use a map and report FOTY0013. Additional numeric bounds, timezone, QName binding, array atomization and wrong-source-type cases are documented in the README. Testing one lexical sample per type does not establish exhaustive XML Schema casting conformance.

**Pinned contract review:** [F&O source e7ee4ab8](https://github.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/blob/e7ee4ab8cb6c6c0f6f60014e2367f1a90909e69e/specifications/xpath-functions-40/src/xpath-functions.xml), sections `constructor-functions-for-xsd-types`, `constructor-functions-for-xsd-list-types`, `constructor-functions-for-xsd-union-types`, plus QName rules. Default argument is the context item; list/union contracts remain distinct. This current comparison does not recover the historically adopted pin. sections.1:
**Hexadecimal/binary integer literals and underscore separators** - **Frozen 4.0**, REQ-118 S3. Lowercase `0x` and `0b` introduce integer literals. Separators are permitted inside decimal, hexadecimal and binary digit groups, including the fraction and exponent groups of decimal/double literals. Ordinary XPath 3.0/3.1 syntax remains available; these extensions require 4.0.

Current comparison: [immutable grammar](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt4cg/qtspecs/b4723ff52fd9d4fabf2b4cd33bd44f21939c512c/specifications/grammar-40/xpath-grammar.xml), productions NumericLiteral, HexIntegerLiteral, BinaryIntegerLiteral, DecimalLiteral, DoubleLiteral, Digits, HexDigits and BinaryDigits. Upstream master was refreshed on 23 October 2026 at this revision. It is a current comparison pin, not a recovered historical adoption pin. [Delivery audit](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md) separates the existing syntax from the source1.23.7 boundary correction; public release remains1.23.4.
sections.6: The prefixes resemble C-family source literals; the exact XPath grammar governs the boundaries. Repeated internal underscores such as `1__000` and `0xFF__FF` are valid under the pinned draft. Each nonempty digit group starts and ends in a digit: `1._2`, `1.2_` and `1e_2` are invalid. A sign is a unary operator, not part of the integer token. Source separators do not extend the XML Schema lexical forms accepted by xs:integer: `xs:integer('1_000')` and `xs:integer('0xFF')` still fail FORG0001.
sections.11: The supplied checks cover integer/decimal/double identity, a value above Int64 range, negative unary application, numeric map/array lookup keys, valid internal repeated separators, malformed groups, wrong radix digits and version refusals. Bosak uses bounded .NET numeric representations; one above-Int64 example does not certify arbitrary-precision integer/decimal support. Other numeric adjacency, Unicode digit and overflow behavior is outside this bounded correction. No performance improvement is claimed.
sections.12: Fifty new catalog cases use the existing public CatalogExampleTests execution path. Initial38 probes produced30 passes and8 failures: malformed fractional/exponent underscore groups were accepted. Source1.23.7 rejects those groups only in the 4.0 lexer path. Thirty-four dedicated API cases cover those eight shapes in all four compatibility levels and valid-group controls in both4.0 profiles. Expected outcomes were not weakened. [Audit and retained evidence](../NUMERIC-LITERALS.md).

sections.6: This is XPath's annotation-driven reconstruction, not JavaScript object spread or an unrestricted immutable dictionary update. Undeclared fields and noncoercible values fail. A cast may discard surplus keys and convert a lexical string to an integer; update uses coercion and therefore does not automatically perform that lexical cast. Optional empty values are entries whose values are empty, not absent keys. Structural records are distinct from XSLT-defined nominal identity.
sections.11: Unknown fields, a plain-map left operand, a non-map right operand and an empty required field raise XPTY0004 in the supplied probes. Integer-to-double promotion is checked; arbitrary string-to-integer update casting is not implied. Optional fields may be set to empty while retaining key presence. Nested structural conversion and declaration order are bounded tested cases, not proof of every composite/nominal type combination.

sections.11:
Benefit: Cast the agreed shape to an annotated record before using the record type contract. Tradeoff: the declared compatibility level and edge rules become part of the consumer contract. A plain map is not an annotated record in Bosak. Coercion policy and undeclared fields must be understood before adapting broad payloads.

The [record-contract delivery](../RECORD-CONTRACTS.md) and [complete stock task](../examples/record-contracts/README.md) add bounded value/error comparisons and the separate [record-update entry](record-updates.md).

| Contract | Cast | Coercion / record update |
|---|---|---|
| Extra source key | Discarded when outside the target record fields | Rejected with XPTY0004. |
| String quantity to integer | Cast when required; invalid lexical value raises FORG0001 | A string is not automatically an integer; supplied parameter/update probes raise XPTY0004. |
| Missing optional field | Create a key whose value is empty | Create that present empty entry; it is not absence. |
| Missing/empty required field | XPTY0004 | XPTY0004. |
| Numeric/nested conversion | Keep matching values or apply the field cast | Apply field coercion recursively; tested integer-to-double promotion. |
| Field order | Constrained by the target record | Coercion/recoercion follows field declaration order in the probes. |
| record(*) | Assertion of an already annotated record | A plain map is not itself an annotated record. |
| Changed value | Construct a record | but with reconstructs under the existing annotation; original value remains available. |

These are tested structural cases, not exhaustive casts, nominal static/default fields or host declarations. Source1.23.6 also fixes an earlier-profile inline-signature leak; [the finding](../INLINE-RECORD-TYPE-GATE.md) preserves the original failing3.1 refusals instead of treating them as supported syntax.
